name: OpenAI Agents SDK
what: OpenAI's lightweight, open-source framework for building agents and multi-agent workflows, in Python (openai-agents) and JavaScript/TypeScript (@openai/agents). It covers agents with tools (functions, MCP servers, hosted tools), handoffs, guardrails, human-in-the-loop, sessions, tracing, sandbox agents and realtime/voice agents. Per the README it is provider-agnostic: it supports the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs and 100+ other LLMs. MIT licensed.
who: Python developers building their own agents who want a small, well-documented framework.

setup.code:
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install openai-agents

setup.text: Set OPENAI_API_KEY and run a first agent:
setup.code:
from agents import Agent, Runner

agent = Agent(name="Assistant", instructions="You are a helpful assistant")
result = Runner.run_sync(agent, "Write a haiku about recursion in programming.")
print(result.final_output)

setup.text: JavaScript/TypeScript equivalent of the first agent (after npm install @openai/agents zod):
Optional Python extras: pip install 'openai-agents[voice]' for voice pipelines and pip install 'openai-agents[redis]' for Redis-backed sessions. Docs: openai.github.io/openai-agents-python.

prompts: Build a triage agent with the OpenAI Agents SDK that hands off to a billing agent or a support agent.
Add an input guardrail that blocks requests unrelated to our product.
Connect my agent to a local MCP server and list the tools it can see.

seo.title: OpenAI Agents SDK: install, quickstart & what it is
seo.description: The OpenAI Agents SDK explained: Python and JavaScript/TypeScript install commands, a first agent, handoffs, guardrails, MCP tools, sessions and tracing.

sections.heading: Agents SDK vs the OpenAI SDK
paragraphs: People often search for "OpenAI SDK" and mean one of two things. The openai package is OpenAI's general API client. The OpenAI Agents SDK is a separate package (openai-agents for Python, @openai/agents for JavaScript/TypeScript) that adds the agent loop, handoffs, guardrails, sessions and tracing on top of model calls.
The Agents SDK docs include a section on when to use the Agents SDK and when to call the Responses API directly. A single model call with no tools or handoffs doesn't need an agent framework.

sections.heading: JavaScript / TypeScript version
paragraphs: There is a separate repository, openai/openai-agents-js. Its README lists Node.js 22 or later, Deno and Bun as supported environments, with Cloudflare Workers (nodejs_compat enabled) as experimental.

faq.q: What is the OpenAI Agents SDK?
faq.a: An open-source framework from OpenAI for building agents and multi-agent workflows. An agent is a model configured with instructions, tools, guardrails and handoffs, and the SDK runs the loop that calls tools and passes work between agents.

faq.q: How do I install the OpenAI Agents SDK?
faq.a: For Python 3.10 or newer, run pip install openai-agents (or uv add openai-agents) and set OPENAI_API_KEY. For JavaScript/TypeScript, run npm install @openai/agents zod.

faq.q: Does it only work with OpenAI models?
faq.a: No. The README describes it as provider-agnostic: it supports the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs and 100+ other LLMs. You still need credentials for whichever provider you use.
Yes. The README lists MCP among the tool types, next to function tools and hosted tools.

faq.q: Is it the same as the openai package?
faq.a: No. The openai package is the general API client. The Agents SDK is a separate package built for agent workflows.
The SDK is MIT licensed and free to use. Model calls to OpenAI or another provider are billed by that provider.
